key_insight: Instead of reusing a fixed class/text embedding at every diffusion step, the paper predicts the next embedding and uses that as conditioning. This makes image generation more adaptive by treating the clean image embedding as the natural continuation of the noisy-image context.
problem_solved: Diffusion transformers usually depend on a condition embedding that is embedded once and reused throughout denoising, which may be too static to guide generation effectively. The paper explores how to replace this fixed conditioning with predicted continuous embeddings that better match the evolving generation process.
method: Introduce Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA), a Transformer trained to predict the next continuous embedding in a sequence.
Use the image generation setup as a sequence problem, where the clean image embedding is predicted after the noisy image and the conditioning input.
During denoising, feed predicted embeddings back as conditioning signals instead of relying on a single fixed class label or text embedding.
impact: This approach could improve how diffusion models condition on context, potentially leading to more flexible and informative generation. For practitioners, it offers a new way to design conditioning mechanisms that better align with the step-by-step nature of image synthesis.
